correctness.rationale: In odd extraspecial p-groups, if idempotent f has nonabelian image then ker f meets the characteristic center trivially; normality implies ker f=1, so f=id. Each proper image is elementary abelian and disjoint from Z. Its image S in symplectic W=G/Z must be isotropic and, for exponent-p² groups, lie in the kernel of the nonzero linear p-power form ℓ. Each such r-space has p^r complements H to Z and p^{r(2n-r)} projections W→S inducing retractions, giving c_r=p^{r(2n-r+1)} times its permitted-isotropic-space count. Symplectic I(n,r) and hyperplane B(n,r)=I(n−1,r−1)+p^rI(n−1,r) yield the two spectra and rank-one gap p^{4n−1}. Independent n=1 count checks give (38,11) for p3 and (152,27) for p5. Finite examples do not establish the all-n counting theorem.

originality.rationale: The full 2019 Anil Kumar–Pradhan article analyzes endomorphism semigroups of extraspecial p-groups and already gives total endomorphism formulas and symplectic isotropic-subspace counts. We credit those inputs. The audited claim restricts to composition-idempotents, classifies all proper group retracts and counts individual rank fibers and subgroup lifts for both odd extraspecial types, including a rank-one type obstruction. No directly covering idempotent spectrum was located in the inspected source.
residual_risks: The published full endomorphism classification might permit a compact derived idempotent count under alternative semigroup terminology; no exact prior statement identified.

value.rationale: Idempotent endomorphisms are canonical retract projections of finite groups. Their exact rank distributions and image subgroup multiplicities in both odd extraspecial types give an interpretable invariant of the endomorphism monoid and distinguish groups with equal order; worthwhile as a natural uniform complete classification rather than a single sample count.

scientific_limitations: Only odd prime p, both extraspecial types order p^{2n+1}, n≥1.
Characteristic 2 has quadratic power obstruction and is excluded.
